## Public Budgeting & Finance Exercises

These interactive, browser-based tutorials are designed for MPA/Public Administration courses in budgeting and finance. Each exercise is a self-contained HTML application — no software installation required. Students work hands-on in Excel or Google Sheets, then use the tutorial to verify their work, get progressive hints, and explore discussion questions grounded in real-world case studies.

All exercises share a common design: downloadable starter spreadsheets, three levels of progressive hints, quick-check and file-upload verification, answer keys, and guided discussion questions.

<div class="exercise-card l-page" id="ex1">
<h3>Exercise 1: Sales Tax Trend Analysis &amp; Revenue Forecasting</h3>
<div class="exercise-row">
<div class="exercise-details">

<span class="section-label">Skills</span>
<p class="skills-line">CPI-based inflation adjustment, year-over-year percentage change, 12-month moving averages, trendline graphing</p>

<span class="section-label">Data</span>
<p class="skills-line">245 rows of monthly sales tax collections (Oct 2001 &ndash; Feb 2022)</p>

<span class="section-label">Tasks Covered</span>
<ol class="task-list">
<li>Inflation Adjustment &mdash; converting nominal dollars to real dollars using CPI ratio</li>
<li>Year-over-Year Percentage Change &mdash; comparing same month across years</li>
<li>12-Month Moving Average &mdash; smoothing noisy data to reveal trends</li>
<li>Data Visualization &mdash; line charts with trendlines</li>
<li>Discussion &amp; Forecasting &mdash; predicting future collections and justifying assumptions</li>
</ol>

<div class="case-heading">Primary Case Study</div>
<p class="case-summary"><strong>Lubbock, TX &mdash; Sales Tax Forecasting Gone Wrong, Then Right</strong></p>
<p class="case-summary">Lubbock overestimated sales tax revenue by $5M in FY2025, leading to a hiring freeze and spending cuts. By FY2026, conservative budgeting brought collections 6% above target. Students who complete the moving average and percentage change exercises will recognize exactly how analysts could over- or under-estimate &mdash; and the real policy consequences of getting it wrong.</p>

<div class="exercise-card l-page" id="ex2">
<h3>Exercise 2: Waste Water Cost Schedule Analysis</h3>
<div class="exercise-row">
<div class="exercise-details">

<span class="section-label">Skills</span>
<p class="skills-line">Fixed/variable cost identification, average and marginal cost calculation, cost curve graphing, pricing strategy analysis</p>

<span class="section-label">Tasks Covered</span>
<ol class="task-list">
<li>Complete the Cost Schedule &mdash; calculate FC, VC, AC, and MC for wastewater treatment</li>
<li>Graph the Cost Curves &mdash; visualize AC and MC curves, identify minimum efficient scale</li>
<li>MC Pricing &amp; Total Cost Recovery &mdash; evaluate marginal cost pricing efficiency</li>
<li>Cost Recovery Pricing &mdash; calculate per-gallon rates using a 15,000-connection base</li>
<li>Discussion Questions &mdash; U-shaped costs, MC vs. AC pricing tradeoffs, two-part tariffs</li>
</ol>

<div class="case-heading">Primary Case Study</div>
<p class="case-summary"><strong>Billings, MT &mdash; Two-Part Wastewater Rate Structure</strong></p>
<p class="case-summary">Billings (pop. ~120,000) uses a two-part rate structure &mdash; a fixed monthly base charge covering infrastructure overhead plus a volumetric per-gallon charge &mdash; that directly mirrors the pricing concepts students explore in this exercise. <div class="exercise-card l-page" id="ex3">
<h3>Exercise 3: Development Department Budget Trend Analysis</h3>
<div class="exercise-row">
<div class="exercise-details">

<span class="section-label">Skills</span>
<p class="skills-line">Column totals, year-over-year percentage changes, average growth rates, budget extrapolation, balance analysis</p>

<span class="section-label">Tasks Covered</span>
<ol class="task-list">
<li>Column Totals &mdash; compute totals across 6 fiscal years of actuals plus adopted/revised budgets</li>
<li>Annual Percentage Changes &mdash; calculate year-over-year changes for 32 expenditure and 34 revenue line items</li>
<li>Average % Change &amp; Proposed FY8 Budget &mdash; extrapolate trends to build a proposed budget</li>
<li>Budget Worksheet &amp; Balance Analysis &mdash; determine if development fees cover operating expenditures</li>
<li>Discussion Questions &mdash; revenue vs. expenditure trends, target-base budgeting, budget linkages</li>
</ol>

<div class="exercise-cases">

<div class="case-heading">Primary Case Study</div>
<p class="case-summary"><strong>Austin, TX &mdash; Development Services Department Fee Revenue vs. Costs</strong></p>
<p class="case-summary">Austin&rsquo;s Development Services Department handles building permits, plan reviews, and inspections &mdash; the same functions in this exercise. During Austin&rsquo;s building boom (2020&ndash;2023), permit fee revenues surged; when construction cooled, revenues dropped while fixed staffing costs remained. The department has faced recurring debates about whether permit fees cover operating costs &mdash; precisely the policy question in this exercise.</p>
<ul class="case-links">
<li><a href="https://communityimpact.com/austin/south-central-austin/government/2024/07/30/austin-weighs-development-staffing-cuts-as-local-construction-slows/">Austin weighs development staffing cuts as construction slows (Community Impact)</a></li>

<li><a href="https://www.austintexas.gov/sites/default/files/files/Finance/Financial%20Transparency/FY-2026---FY-2030-Five-Year-Financial-Forecast-Report.pdf">FY2026&ndash;2030 Five-Year Financial Forecast (City of Austin PDF)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.binghamgp.com/blog/2024/5/8/bg-blog-austin-budget-review-2024">Austin budget review &mdash; DSD construction slowdown (Bingham GP)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.austintexas.gov/sites/default/files/files/Development_Services/Matrix_Fee_Study_-2015.pdf">DSD fee study &mdash; 56% cost recovery rate (City of Austin PDF)</a></li>
</ul>

<div class="exercise-card l-page" id="ex4">
<h3>Exercise 4: Year-End Budget Monitoring &amp; Projections</h3>
<div class="exercise-row">
<div class="exercise-details">

<span class="section-label">Skills</span>
<p class="skills-line">Three projection formulas (average spending, seasonal, current month), best-estimate selection, variance analysis</p>

<span class="section-label">Tasks Covered</span>
<ol class="task-list">
<li>Average Spending Formula &mdash; YTD / 7 x 12 (assumes uniform monthly spending)</li>
<li>Seasonal &amp; Current Month Formulas &mdash; using last year&rsquo;s pattern and most recent month data</li>
<li>Select Best Estimate &mdash; choose the most appropriate formula per line item</li>
<li>Variance &amp; Budget Comparison &mdash; compute Adopted Budget minus EOY Estimate</li>
</ol>

<div class="exercise-cases">

<div class="case-heading">Primary Case Study</div>
<p class="case-summary"><strong>Stockton, CA &mdash; When Budget Monitoring Fails</strong></p>
<p class="case-summary">Stockton failed to track how actual spending commitments (generous pensions, a $47M arena, rising personnel costs) aligned with sustainable revenue. The gap grew over years until bankruptcy was the only option. The three projection formulas students apply in this exercise are the same type of basic monitoring that would have flagged Stockton&rsquo;s growing fiscal crisis.</p>
<ul class="case-links">
<li><a href="https://www.npr.org/2012/07/20/157105483/for-stockton-calif-bankruptcy-freezes-everything">For Stockton, bankruptcy freezes everything (NPR, 2012)</a></li>

<li><a href="https://www.npr.org/2012/03/11/148384030/an-example-to-avoid-city-of-stockton-on-the-brink">An example to avoid: City of Stockton on the brink (NPR, 2012)</a></li>
</ul>

<div class="exercise-card l-page" id="ex5">
<h3>Exercise 5: Budgeting for Debt Service Using Constant Principal</h3>
<div class="exercise-row">
<div class="exercise-details">

<span class="section-label">Skills</span>
<p class="skills-line">Debt service schedule construction, SUMPRODUCT-based interest, NIC/TIC calculation, I&amp;S tax rate analysis</p>

<span class="section-label">Tasks Covered</span>
<ol class="task-list">
<li>Compute Interest &amp; Debt Service &mdash; build the full annual payment schedule</li>
<li>Calculate Bond Metrics &mdash; bond-years, average life, Net Interest Cost (NIC), True Interest Cost (TIC via IRR)</li>
<li>I&amp;S Tax Rate &amp; Debt Capacity &mdash; determine a tax rate needed to fund debt service</li>
<li>Visualize the Debt Schedule &mdash; chart principal, interest, and total payments over time</li>
</ol>

<div class="btn-row">
<a class="launch-btn" href="https://mro0001.github.io/exercise5-debt-service/">Launch Tutorial</a>
<a class="repo-link" href="https://github.com/mro0001/exercise5-debt-service">GitHub Repository</a>
</div>

</div>
<div class="exercise-cases">

<div class="case-heading">Primary Case Study</div>
<p class="case-summary"><strong>Harvey, IL &mdash; Bond Default and Restructuring</strong></p>
<p class="case-summary">Harvey defaulted on $32M in GO bonds &mdash; the exact instrument students model in this exercise. The city&rsquo;s total debt grew to $164M, far beyond any reasonable I&amp;S rate capacity. When students calculate Year 1 debt service of $1,418,600 for a well-managed $20M bond, they can contrast that with Harvey&rsquo;s inability to make any payments at all. Every metric students calculate (debt service, NIC, I&amp;S rate) is a metric Harvey&rsquo;s analysts should have been tracking.</p>
<ul class="case-links">
<li><a href="https://www.bondbuyer.com/news/harvey-illinois-declares-itself-financially-distressed">Harvey declares itself financially distressed (Bond Buyer, Oct 2025)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.bondbuyer.com/news/harvey-illinois-finally-seals-deal-on-bond-default-litigation">Harvey seals deal on bond default litigation (Bond Buyer, Aug 2023)</a></li>

<li><a href="https://www.illinoispolicy.org/harvey-declaring-financial-distress-under-164m-debt/">Harvey declaring financial distress under $164M debt (Illinois Policy)</a></li>
</ul>
